doctrine.title: Mood Board Operating Doctrine
doctrine.purpose: Visual alignment and communication tool — locks shared understanding of look, feel, tone before a shoot or project begins. Prevents mid-project drift and shortens approval cycles.
doctrine.core_principle: A mood board is not inspiration collection. It is a decision document. Every element on it answers: what are we making, for whom, and why does it feel this way.

methodologies.name: Color-First Assembly
methodologies.use_when: Brand or editorial work where tonal palette is the creative anchor
steps: Pull 15-20 images from any source (Pinterest, Google Images, stock, personal archive)
Filter down to 6-8 images that share a dominant palette
Arrange in a grid; strip everything else
Extract 3-5 hex codes as the palette lock

methodologies.name: Typography + Design Element Assembly
methodologies.use_when: Brand identity, logo, or print work where type is the primary visual voice
steps: Collect type specimens alongside layout references
Group by weight and register (sans vs serif, editorial vs corporate)
Board must answer: what font family, what weight range, what tracking register

methodologies.name: Photography Direction Board
methodologies.use_when: Pre-shoot alignment with talent, MUA, stylists, and clients
key_elements: Wardrobe texture and silhouette (not literal garment)
Camera-to-subject distance and lens compression reference
methodologies.note: Each element should have ONE image that is the locked reference, not a mood cluster. Ambiguity at the board level produces ambiguity on set.

methodologies.name: Product Photography Board
methodologies.use_when: Commercial product shoots requiring surface, context, and lighting lock
elements: Lighting style (hard vs soft, natural vs studio)
Composition style (flat lay vs 3/4 vs hero angle)

methodologies.name: AI-Assisted Pre-Viz Board
methodologies.use_when: Composite builds, generative environment tests, or client concept approval before production
workflow: Use 6-component prompt structure: subject + action + environment + art style + lighting + details
Generate 8-12 variants in Midjourney or comparable tool
Select 2-3 that match the direction; add to board alongside real references
Test personalization by generating known-style references and rating output fidelity
Shortlist by stripping color to evaluate composition and tonal structure alone

genre_prompt_anchors.portrait: subject, expression register, lighting quality, background separation, skin tonal target
genre_prompt_anchors.product: surface, background, light source angle, shadow style
genre_prompt_anchors.architecture: viewpoint, ambient vs artificial light ratio, time of day
genre_prompt_anchors.landscape: atmospheric depth, foreground anchor, sky treatment
genre_prompt_anchors.street: focal plane, motion treatment, ambient light color temperature
genre_prompt_anchors.abstract: texture register, color relationship, geometric vs organic

tool_stack.discord_shortcuts: Midjourney supports custom Discord shortcuts for frequently used style prompts — set these up for recurring aesthetic registers to cut prompt time

direction_tactics_for_photographers: Never show the client a mood board with more than 12 images — cognitive overload collapses alignment
Label each image with a one-word descriptor of WHY it's on the board (not what it shows)
Lock lighting reference first; everything else is subordinate
Separate 'color grade target' from 'lighting reference' — conflating them creates post-production confusion
For composite work: build two boards — one for the subject capture environment, one for the background environment
Show what you are NOT making alongside what you are making; the contrast sharpens the brief
midjourney_personalization_workflow: Generate 20-30 images in your target aesthetic using explicit prompts
Rate each (accept/reject) to build a style model
Run a mood board batch using the personalization code appended to prompts
Compare rated outputs against the mood board; promote or reject the personalization model
Custom Discord shortcuts store your top prompt templates for fast re-use

sniped_application.direction_stack_fit: Mood boards are the client-facing artifact of the Direction Stack. The board operationalizes the stack's language into visual proof that you speak the client's aesthetic before the shoot.
sniped_application.composite_environment_rotation: Each of the 7 composite environments (Brutalist Monument / Industrial Minimal / Monochromatic Void / Sculptural Gallery / Cinematic Urban / Organic Surreal / Futurist Editorial) should have a standing mood board that is rebuilt per chapter, not per shoot.
sniped_application.pre_shoot_prep_integration: Mood board delivery is a gate in the pre-shoot prep doctrine — board approved = shoot confirmed. No board = no shoot date locked.
sniped_application.ai_as_world_construction: AI generation tools belong on the composite/environment board only. Identity (subject face/body) references must be real photography. This enforces the edit-register bifurcation rule: AI for world-construction, anti-AI on identity.

notes: Source is a raw document dump of transcribed video tutorials and Reddit discussions (85% boilerplate, 15% actionable). Segments 1-10 cover design-discipline mood boarding; segments 11-12 cover AI tool workflows (Kling/Runway transitions, Midjourney personalization, 6-component prompting). All content is instructional with no original strategic frameworks. Signal rated medium: actionable tool knowledge and photography-direction tactics extracted, but no methodology unique to SNIPED or beyond what a competent practitioner already knows.
